english.title: Sub-let / part with possession of a dwelling-house let under an assured tenancy in breach of a term of the tenancy

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: prevention of social housing fraud act 2013

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a tenant of a dwelling-house let under an assured tenancy to which section 2 of the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ADDRESS..), in breach of an express or implied term of the tenancy,

(A)_[sub-let]_
(B)_[parted with possession of]_

(C)_[the whole of the dwelling-house,]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 2(1) and (6) of the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013.

english.notes:
(i) Section 2 of the Prevention of Social Housing Fraud Act 2013 applies to an assured tenancy -
(a) under which the landlord is a private registered provider of social housing or a registered social landlord, and (b) which is not a shared ownership lease.

(ii) This offence is not committed where the tenant takes the action described in paragraphs 2(1)(a) and 2(1)(b) because of violence or threats of violence by a person residing in, or in the locality of, the dwelling-house -
(a) towards the tenant, or -
(b) towards a member of the family of the tenant who was residing with the tenant immediately before the tenant ceased to occupy the dwelling-house. .

(iii) The offence is not committed if a person ("P") who occupies the dwelling-house as a result of the conduct described in subsection 2(1)(a) is -
(a) a person entitled to apply to the court for an order giving P a right to occupy the dwelling-house or to have the tenancy transferred to P, or
(b) a person in respect of whom an application may be made to have the tenancy transferred to P or to another person to be held for P's benefit.

(iv) An unlawful profit order may be made by a court in relation to a defendant convicted of this offence - see section 4 of the Act for further details.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex (see section 3 of the Act)

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
